Good afternoon Jeffrey Barney, Brandon Lance, Mathew Draper, Gustavo Rodas, Zack Kurtz,
 
I want to make sure we are prioritizing the sorting of almonds for L1. It is imperative that we keep this line running and maintain a strong pass down from shift to shift. Almond sorting should be treated like any other production line, with the goal of keeping it running continuously so the next shift can take over without interruption.
We should have three people assigned to sorting at all times:

Person 1: Dump almonds into the sorter.Person 2: Fill buckets with sorted almonds.Person 3: Manage scrap, level out the tote, and keep the area clean and organized.
When a tote becomes empty:

One person takes the tote to be weighed, makes sure all paperwork is filled out correctly.The other two people immediately swap in the empty tote and begin sorting the next tote.This will help minimize downtime and maintain a continuous flow.
For lunch breaks:

Only one person goes at a time.The other two team members should continue sorting.Employees should time their lunches appropriately so they are not away when a tote change is needed.
Finally, finished totes must be wrapped, labeled, and sent to L1 immediately upon completion. Avoid allowing completed totes to sit in the sorting area. 
 
Our priority is to keep L1 supplied and running efficiently through consistent sorting operations and effective communication between shifts.
 
Please share with your teams and make sure this is followed.
